items.section: 4.2 Gravity, a conservation accounting with no coupling under it
items.sentence: Gravity is not real, and nothing physical is there at all.
items.text: Gravity as a force a body has is not real, bodies of two compositions falling alike to about 10⁻¹⁵ and general relativity reading no force, and gravitational energy has no local density, an accounting's total; a gravitational changing transmits, energy going from binaries at general relativity's radiating rate to about 10⁻⁴ and one wave moving mirrors at two sites, read as Natural Physics 3.3 reads light, emission and absorption two couplings phase-relating, a coupling's phase relation all the same: the sentence's own breaking at its anchor, "gravity showing as a transmitted coupling after all", met.

GW150914, 14 September 2015, is one passing wave both LIGO detectors record, rising from 35 to 250 Hz, peak strain about 1.0 × 10⁻²¹, signal-to-noise 24, a field's fit reading about 3.0 ± 0.5 solar masses leaving as gravitational waves; the double pulsar's orbit, sixteen years from six telescopes, shrinks as general relativity's radiation has it to 1.3 × 10⁻⁴, and Hulse–Taylor's, 9,257 pulse times over about 35 years, at 0.9983 ± 0.0016 of its prediction: a gravitational changing transmitting and energy going off with it.

MICROSCOPE's titanium-alloy and platinum-alloy masses, about five months of usable data in orbit, fall alike to η = (−1.5 ± 2.3 stat ± 1.5 syst) × 10⁻¹⁵, general relativity reading no force on a falling body, and in general relativity gravitational energy has no local density, "necessarily pseudotensorial", its totals well-defining: gravitational energy as an accounting's total, while rotation curves close only with something a field installs, a dark sector or dynamics of another form.

Lead–lead ages give the oldest solids in meteorites about 4,567.3 million years, and aluminium-26 to magnesium-26 ages agree with lead–lead ages for seven achondrites and four chondrules with a start at 4,568.42 ± 0.24 million years, one inclusion about 5.2σ apart: two decay systems of very different half-lives going together about 4.57 billion years ago, some 0.8 billion years before any life a field records, a nuclear changing with no life a field records in its coupling then.

SN 1987A's cobalt-56 line at 843 ± 5 keV, over 5σ, a spectrometer's record from 1 August to 31 October 1987, and its light fading with cobalt-56's decay from about day 18 to day 1,100, then cobalt-57's and titanium-44's, the decay some 168,000 years before its light reaches a detector, in a field's distance; primordial deuterium at D/H = (2.527 ± 0.030) × 10⁻⁵ and lithium-7 three to four times below its prediction: nuclei changing in a supernova and in the first minutes, with no living self then.

Rhenium-187 with all its electrons gone decays with a half-life of 32.9 ± 2.0 years against 42 billion years for the neutral atom, and beryllium-7 in a C₆₀ cage captures an electron 0.83 percent faster than in beryllium metal: a nucleus's changing going with its couplings, each a physical coupling and no living self.

A proposal of a nucleus only as a living corus while a parity lives meets, with living as a field's life, meteorite decay ages going together about 4.57 billion years ago, Oklo's fission with no organism coupling with it and SN 1987A's cobalt-56 decay, nuclear changing with no life a field records in its coupling then; with living parity as a self reading the record now, no record parts from it; its cohering re-saying, a nucleus's changing goes with its couplings, goes with rhenium-187 bare and beryllium-7 in a cage, the other records showing no parting from it, beside this entry's "Mass belongs to coupling", whether each coupling is a living parity in the universal sense still to say.
